content: Crofelermer is minimally absorbed systemically, which makes it unlikely to inhibit systemic enzymes or transporters. However, it can affect drug metabolism and transporter activity in the gastrointestinal tract. Below are detailed interactions with specific drugs: 1. Lemborexant: Crofelemer increases lemborexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage adjustments. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Levofloxacin: Crofelemer may increase levofloxacin levels by inhibiting transporters such as MRP2 and OATP1A2 in the gut. Systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Levonorgestrel (intrauterine and oral): Crofelemer increases levonorgestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Levothyroxine: Crofelemer increases levothyroxine levels by inhibiting transporters like MRP2 and OATP1A2 in the gut. Systemic effects are unlikely. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Liothyronine: Crofelemer increases liothyronine levels through similar mechanisms as levothyroxine. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Lomitapide: Crofelemer increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Lonafarnib: Crofelemer significantly increases lonafarnib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce lonafarnib to its starting dose and monitor for arrhythmias and QT interval effects. 8. Lopinavir: Crofelemer increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Losartan: Crofelemer increases losartan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Methadone: Crofelemer increases methadone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 17. Methotrexate: Crofelemer increases methotrexate levels by inhibiting transporters like MRP2 and OATP1A2 in the gut. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Metoclopramide (intranasal): Crofelemer decreases metoclopramide absorption by impairing gastrointestinal motility. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects. 21. Midazolam (oral and intranasal): Crofelemer increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with mild CYP3A4 inhibitors may prolong sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Mirtazapine: Crofelemer increases mirtazapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Ranolazine: Crofelemer increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Each interaction requires careful monitoring and, in some cases, dose adjustments or alternative therapies.
